classification.difficultyReason: Students transfer an exact height between two right triangles and explain the effect of premature rounding.

content.prompt: For this 3D diagram, complete these steps.

spec.description: Two triangles share vertical AB. Only A and B are named. Both ground-side right-angle markers and both angle sectors are retained; ordinary blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: Ground lengths 10 m and 8 m; AB is perpendicular to each; left elevation angle 29 degrees and right elevation angle theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Height AB and theta remain unknown.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Why is it important to keep values in exact form and only round the final answer? Try finding $\theta$ by rounding $AB$ to 1 d.p. and using the rounded result.

answer.short: Rounding too early can change the final rounded answer. Using $AB\approx5.5\text{ m}$ gives $\theta\approx34.5^\circ$, which is $0.2^\circ$ below the answer without intermediate rounding.
answer.worked:
Rounding an intermediate value introduces an error that can affect the final answer.
$$\begin{aligned}AB&=10\tan29^\circ\\AB&\approx5.5\text{ m}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5.5}{8}\right)\\\theta&\approx34.5^\circ\end{aligned}$$
This is $0.2^\circ$ below $34.7^\circ$, the answer obtained without rounding the intermediate height.
